logline: A constrained politician's daughter who manages a luxury hotel meets a free-spirited young traveler in Cuba - and when he turns up as her employee in Seoul, they must navigate a relationship that defies everything their worlds allow.

renewal.note: Single-season limited series. 16 episodes aired on tvN from November 28, 2018 to January 24, 2019. Broadcasting rights sold to over 100 territories.

bollymeter.basis: The premiere drew 8.7% nationwide ratings, among the highest cable drama debuts of 2018. Broadcasting rights sold to over 100 territories. Critics noted Song Hye-kyo and Park Bo-gum were 'completely absorbed in their roles' in a quietly composed melodrama.

seasons.review_body: Encounter (also known as Boyfriend) is a measured, visually precise melodrama that trades on the contrast between its leads' social worlds. Cha Soo-hyun lives inside duty - political family, public role, watched life. Kim Jin-hyuk lives inside spontaneity. Their Cuba meeting is the kind of meet-cute that could feel contrived, but director Park Shin-woo shoots it as something closer to collision than coincidence. Song Hye-kyo delivers one of her quieter, more technically controlled performances; Park Bo-gum matches her restraint without losing warmth. The 8.7% premiere rating placed it among cable television's highest launches that year, with broadcasting rights sold to over 100 territories. The series rewards viewers who prefer atmosphere over plot.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Cuba sequence that opens the series sets a visual and tonal register the rest of the show has to live up to - and mostly does. The contrast between the sunlit Havana backdrop and the closed Seoul world awaiting both leads is established without commentary.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first real conversation between Soo-hyun and Jin-hyuk, in which neither says what they mean and both know it.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale lands the relationship arc cleanly but the resolution of the political subplot feels compressed relative to the care the show lavished on the romantic beats in earlier episodes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Soo-hyun's choice in the final scene - which lands as a statement of self rather than a conventional romance ending.
